newsitem.title: UK: British film makers to enjoy tax break.
newsitem.headline: British film makers to enjoy tax break.

text.p: The British government gave the country's flourishing cinema industry a fresh boost on Wednesday when it introduced tax breaks for domestic film productions.
Finance minister Gordon Brown announced that production and acquisition costs on British films with budgets of up to 15 million pounds ($25 million) would qualify for a 100 percent tax write-off.

"It's incredibly exciting for the government to immediately give the film industry the one thing it has been demanding for a number of years," said Stewart Till, head of the international division of PolyGram Filmed Entertainment (PFE).
PFE, part of global music and film giant PolyGram NV, has been associated with low budget British film hits such as "Four Weddings And A Funeral" and "Trainspotting" in recent years.

Till, co-chairman of a film policy review unit set up by the British government last month, said the move announced by Brown in his budget was a "shot in the arm for an industry already showing great signs of life".
Some 90 million pounds of national lottery money have been earmarked for British film makers in an attempt to help turn a cottage industry into a global force.
Chancellor Brown said the tax break would cost 30 million pounds over three years. He said he hoped that it would boost British film exports.
"The talents of British film makers can and should, wherever possible, be employed to the benefit of the British economy," Brown said in his budget speech. ($ = 0.602 British Pounds)
